content: 1. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 3. Efavirenz and cannabidiol interact via hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Due to potential induction and inhibition of CYP2B6, dosage adjustments of CYP2B6 substrates may be necessary. 4. Carbamazepine reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Cariprazine and efavirenz both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of celecoxib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 8. Cenobamate also decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Efavirenz and cenobamate both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are required. 10. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of chlorpheniramine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 13. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, efavirenz increases cilostazol toxicity by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 15. Efavirenz and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Efavirenz and cisapride both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of clobazam by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 19. Efavirenz and clobazam both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Efavirenz and clomipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 21. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of clonazepam by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Clonidine and efavirenz both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are required. 23. Efavirenz decreases the efficacy of clopidogrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of clorazepate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of clozapine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 27. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of conivaptan by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 28. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of cortisone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Efavirenz increases the levels of crizotinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Crofelemer increases the levels of efavirenz by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 32. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring of cyclosporine concentrations is necessary, especially during the first two weeks of therapy. 34. Dabrafenib reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 35. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of dantrolene by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 36. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of daprodustat. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors increase daprodustat exposure, requiring dose adjustments. 37. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of dapsone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Efavirenz and daridorexant both increase sedation, raising the risk of CNS depression and psychomotor impairment. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 39. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of darifenacin by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 40. Darunavir and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 41. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of dasatinib by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 42. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 43. Efavirenz and degarelix both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 44. Efavirenz and desipramine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Desloratadine and efavirenz both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are required. 46. Efavirenz and deutetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 47. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 48. Dexbrompheniramine and efavirenz both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are required. 49. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of diazepam by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of diclofenac by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 52. Didanosine and efavirenz increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of liver toxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. 53. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 54. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of docetaxel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 55. Efavirenz and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of donepezil by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 57. Efavirenz and doxepin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 59. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 60. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 61. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 62. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is not recommended. 63. Efavirenz and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 64. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of erlotinib by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 65. Erythromycin increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 66. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 67. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 68. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 69. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 70. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised.
